1. (Currently Amended) A cell comprising: a non-native compartment comprising a proteinaceous shell comprising at least one bacterial microcompartment (BMC) polypeptide, wherein the non-native compartment is __engineered to contain a heterologous enzyme not naturally associated with the BMC polypeptide__.

2. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the non-native compartment is self-assembled in vivo __and comprises BMC polypeptides from at least two different bacterial species__.

3. (Original) The cell of claim 1 wherein the non-native compartment further comprises at least one targeted enzyme.

4. (Original) The cell of claim 3 wherein the non-native compartment comprises a plurality of different targeted enzymes.

5. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 3 or claim 4 wherein the at least one targeted enzyme comprises a compartment-specific targeting signal sequence __and is not naturally present in the same compartment as the BMC polypeptide in its native bacterial source__.

6. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the BMC polypeptide comprises a Eut polypeptide __and the cell is not Clostridium freundii__.

7. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 6 wherein the Eut polypeptide comprises a EutS polypeptide __and the cell is not Clostridium freundii__.

8. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the proteinaceous shell comprises a plurality of different BMC polypeptides __derived from different bacterial species or different BMC operons__.

9. (Original) The cell of claim 8 wherein the plurality of different BMC polypeptides comprises BMC polypeptides from different bacterial species.

10. (Original) The cell of claim 8 wherein the plurality of different BMC polypeptides comprises BMC polypeptides from different BMC operons.

11. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein at least one BMC polypeptide comprises an affinity tag __for purification purposes__.

12. (Currently Amended) A method comprising: introducing into a host cell a polynucleotide that encodes at least one BMC polypeptide and at least one heterologous enzyme not naturally associated with the BMC polypeptide, thereby producing a transformed cell; and growing the transformed cell under conditions effective for the transformed cell to express the polynucleotide that encodes at least one BMC polypeptide and produce a non-native compartment comprising a proteinaceous shell comprising the at least one BMC polypeptide __and the at least one heterologous enzyme, wherein the compartment is engineered to contain metabolic activity not present in the native bacterial source of the BMC polypeptide__.

13. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises a bacterium __other than the native bacterial source of the BMC polypeptide__.

14. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13 wherein the bacterium comprises a member of the family Enterobacteriaceae __and the BMC polypeptide is derived from a different bacterial species__.

15. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 14 wherein the member of the family Enterobacteriaceae comprises E. coli __and the BMC polypeptide is not derived from E. coli__.

16. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13 wherein the bacterium comprises a member of the family Shewanellaceae __and the BMC polypeptide is derived from a different bacterial species__.

17. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises a yeast __and the BMC polypeptide is derived from a bacterium__.

18. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 17 wherein the yeast comprises a member of the family Saccharomycetaceae __and the BMC polypeptide is derived from a bacterium__.

19. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 18 wherein the member of the family Saccharomycetaceae comprises Saccharomyces cerevisiae __and the BMC polypeptide is derived from a bacterium__.

20. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises an alga __and the BMC polypeptide is derived from a bacterium__.

21. (Currently Amended) A method comprising: providing a cell comprising a non-native compartment comprising: a proteinaceous shell comprising at least one bacterial microcompartment (BMC) polypeptide derived from a first bacterial source, and at least one enzyme that catalyzes conversion of a substrate to a product, wherein the enzyme is not naturally associated with the BMC polypeptide in its native bacterial source; and growing the cell under conditions effective for the at least one enzyme to catalyze conversion of the substrate to a product __within the non-native compartment__.

22. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a bioactive product __not naturally produced by the native bacterial source of the BMC polypeptide__.

23. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a drug or a drug precursor __not naturally produced by the native bacterial source of the BMC polypeptide__.

24. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a biofuel or a precursor of biofuel production __not naturally produced by the native bacterial source of the BMC polypeptide__.

25. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the at least one enzyme catalyzes a step in degrading or detoxifying a toxic substrate __and the enzyme is not naturally present in the same compartment as the BMC polypeptide in its native bacterial source__.

26. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 further comprising isolating at least a portion of the non-native compartments __from the host cell__.

27. (Original) The method of claim 26 wherein at least a portion of the non-native compartment comprise an affinity tag and isolating at least a portion of the non-native compartments comprises contacting a sample comprising the non-native compartments with an affinity substrate having selective affinity for the affinity tag.

28. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 comprising a plurality of compartments __each comprising BMC polypeptides from different bacterial sources or different BMC operons__.
